item.title: Watch: 2026 Ballon d'Or winner Harry Kane makes Virat Kohli admission after 'starstruck' question
item.description: England footballer Harry Kane was asked about whether he was left "starstruck" by any congratulatory message following his historic Ballon d'Or victory. The striker revealed he had recieved multiple messages from sportspersons, including Indian cricket legend Virat Kohli . "People like David Beckham, who is a big idol of mine, have messaged me. Tom Brady, Virat Kohli, you know..a lot of sports people I really admire and look up to," Kane told reporters. Watch: — Melbourne__82 (@Melbourne__82) Kane won the 2026 Ballon d'Or at a ceremony held at the London Palladium on October 26, becoming the first English footballer in 25 years to receive the prestigious award. The Bayern Munich striker narrowly beat Kylian Mbappé, collecting 1,055 points compared to the Frenchman's 1,027. Lamine Yamal was also among the leading contenders. The England captain enjoyed an outstanding 2025-26 season, scoring 73 goals across all competitions for Bayern Munich. His performances helped him secure the biggest individual honour in football. However, a special message from Kohli made the occasion even more memorable for him. Harry Kane reveals Virat Kohli's special message Kane admitted that receiving congratulations from Kohli was a surprising and memorable moment. Despite being one of football's biggest stars himself, he was impressed to hear from the Indian batter, whom he has admired for a long time. Kohli is widely regarded as one of the greatest cricketers of his generation. His popularity extends beyond cricket, with several international sporting personalities recognising his achievements and influence. The Indian star's famous unbeaten 82 off 51 balls against Australia in the 2016 T20 World Cup remains one of the most memorable performances of his career. His ability to deliver under pressure has earned him admirers across different sports. How did Kane and Kohli develop mutual respect? The connection between Kane and Kohli goes back several years. The two sporting icons reportedly met in London in May 2019, helping establish a mutual admiration for each other's achievements. Kohli's congratulatory message was therefore more than just a routine gesture for Kane. It came from someone he genuinely respects and admires. Kohli's popularity among international sporting stars is not new. American football legend Tom Brady has also previously spoken about the Indian cricketer's appeal.

item.title: Green Bay Packers receive encouraging Micah Parsons update ahead of Patriots matchup
item.description: The Green Bay Packers found their footing again in Week 8, earning a 27-19 win over the Carolina Panthers. Their defense led the way, and the unit could receive another boost following the team’s latest injury update. Micah Parsons could soon take another step toward returning to the field. ESPN’s Adam Schefter reported that Packers head coach Matt LaFleur said Monday the team is preparing for the star pass rusher to resume practicing this week. Parsons has not played since Green Bay’s December 14, 2025, matchup with Denver, when he suffered a torn ACL. He has been focused on recovering from the injury ever since. Having Parsons back for Sunday’s matchup with the Patriots would give Green Bay a major lift. Still, his expected return to practice does not necessarily mean he will be cleared for game action right away. Reports have pointed to the Packers’ Thanksgiving Eve meeting with the Rams as a more realistic target for his return. Will Micah Parsons finally return for the Green Bay Packers? Green Bay Packers defensive end Parsons (1), linebacker Edgerrin Cooper (56) and cornerback Keisean Nixon (25) team up to stop Detroit Lions running back Jahmyr Gibbs (0) on Sunday, September 7, 2025, at Lambeau Field in Green Bay, Wis. The Packers won the game, 27-13. Tork Mason/USA TODAY NETWORK-Wisconsin The timing would work in Green Bay’s favor, as the Packers have their bye week immediately before that matchup. A return to practice this week would give Parsons several weeks to build up before potentially being activated for Week 12. Although he would miss a significant portion of the season, he could still appear in seven regular season games. Even with that limited window, Parsons could provide a major boost as Green Bay pushes for a playoff spot. Green Bay Packers defensive end Parsons (1) interacts with fans before a game against the Chicago Bears on Sunday, Oct. 11, 2026, at Lambeau Field in Green Bay, Wisconsin. The Packers won the game, 31-7. Tork Mason/Green Bay Press-Gazette Green Bay enters the stretch run with a 5-3 record and remains in contention for the NFC North title, despite sitting fourth in the division. The Packers’ Week 10 clash with the Minnesota Vikings could prove crucial as they look to strengthen their position in the NFC playoff race. The Packers will be looking to secure an important win this weekend, regardless of whether Parsons is available. Parsons and the Packers visit the Patriots on November 8, with kickoff set for 4:25 p.m. ET at Gillette Stadium. item.title: College Basketball Rankings: Men’s Top-25 with insight from experts who know their teams best
item.description: UCLA Bruins guard Eric Dailey Jr. (3) drives toward the basket while being defended by San Diego Toreros forward Jose Roberto Tanchyn (14) during an NCAA men's basketball game at Pauley Pavilion in Los Angeles, California, on October 27, 2026. (Photo by Peter Zhan/NurPhoto via Getty Images) | NurPhoto via Getty Images No. 1 Florida There is a very obvious reason why Florida is a lot of people’s choice to earn a No. 1 seed for a third consecutive season and a national title for the second time in three tries. Put simply, college basketball has rarely seen a frontcourt as strong as the one the Gators are going to put on the floor throughout this winter. Thomas Haugh, Alex Condon, and Rueben Chinyelu are all potential All-Americans who give Florida an absurd combination of scoring, size, rebounding, facilitating and interior defense. Haugh returns as a preseason First Team All-American after averaging 17.1 points per game and flirting with the NBA. Condon was a preseason First Team All-American last season, while Chinyelu is likely the best defensive big man in the country. What Todd Golden has that he didn’t have last season is experience and continuity in the backboard. Point guard Boogie Fland really came on in the second half of last season, and is back to run the show again in Gainesville. He’ll be aided by Denzel Aberdeen, a key reserve on the 2024-25 national championship squad who spent last season at Kentucky, and sharp-shooting reserve Urban Klavzar. As long as this group stays healthy (and Aberdeen stays eligible), there just aren’t many weaknesses here for opponents to exploit. — Mike Rutherford No. 2 Duke Duke loses Cameron Boozer, but might still be better, because Jon Scheyer has ridiculous depth and versatility at every position. Some analysts think Pat Ngongba might be the best player in the country; some think he might be second best on this team behind JoJo Boumtje Boumtje. Duke has perhaps the deepest guard rotation in the country with Caleb Foster, John Blackwell, Cayden Boozer, and Deron Rippey. There’s depth at the wings, too, with Dame Sarr, Bryson Howard, and exhibition season breakout star Sebastian Wilkins. All things considered, this might be the deepest team in college since the 2014-15 Kentucky Wildcats. Duke is primed for a major run this year. — JD King, Duke Basketball Report No. 3 Illinois The Illinois Fighting Illini are expected to be one of the best teams in the country again this season following their historic Final Four run last year. The Illini lose three key pieces in Keaton Wagler, Kylan Boswell and Ben Humrichous but will return the other five rotation players from a season ago. David Mirkovic, Tomislav Ivisic, Zvonimir Ivisic, Andrej Stojakovic and Jake Davis are all back, giving Illinois the third-most returning minutes in the Big Ten behind only Minnesota and Michigan State, according to Bart Torvik. Illinois also added one of the best guards in the transfer portal in former Providence guard Stefan Vaak

item.title: Where the Houston Texans rank statistically heading into Week 9?
item.description: From here on out, the Houston Texans must win. Sitting with a mere two victories — albeit against in-division opponents — the Texans can't afford to drop a game moving forward. They're currently 0-4 at Reliant Stadium and have matchups against several losing teams who have already thrown in the towel for 2026. Should a loss come on Sunday against the Los Angeles Chargers, what's left to play for? Houston won't be headed toward the postseason and likely will need to shake up the coaching staff and roster to get back to winning football in 2027. But right now, DeMeco Ryans isn't focused on a potential fire sale before the NFL trade deadline or a run toward the playoffs. Sights are set, following a week off to take care of the Bolts, and moving toward a 3-5 record. “Our opportunity starts this week with us being focused on handling what we can control, controlling what we can control and not putting a focus on a run,” Ryans said. “It's about how do we prepare the right way. How do we play more disciplined? How do we have the self-discipline to go out and play clean football?" With Week 9 here, let's look at how Houston stacks up among all 32 NFL teams entering the regular season. Stats courtesy of Team Rankings , The Football Database , ESPN and PickWatch . item.title: Ranking the Rockies, 2026: No. 29, Gabriel Hughes
item.description: DENVER, CO - SEPTEMBER 18: Colorado Rockies pitcher Gabriel Hughes (43) pitches in the first inning during a game between the Seattle Mariners and the Colorado Rockies at Coors Field on September 18, 2026 in Denver, Colorado. (Photo by Dustin Bradford/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images Welcome to the 2026 edition of Ranking the Rockies, where we take a look back at every player to log playing time for the Rockies in 2026. The purpose of this list is to provide a snapshot of the player in context. The “Ranking” is an organizing principle that’s drawn from Baseball Reference’s WAR (rWAR). It’s not something the staff debated. We’ll begin with the player with the lowest rWAR and end up with the player with the highest. No. 29, Gabriel Hughes (0.1 rWAR) When the Colorado Rockies selected Gabriel Hughes 10th overall out of Gonzaga in the 2022 MLB Draft , they knew they were taking on a power arm with at least a middle-of-the-rotation ceiling. However, after Tommy John surgery cut his 2023 season short and kept him out of the 2024 season, he had to start building his stock in 2025. Hughes had a solid season last year, despite dealing with several injuries throughout the year. Heading into 2026, it seemed like it was inevitable that he would finally reach the big leagues. He finally earned his call-up to the big leagues in early July 2026 , making his Major League debut on July 3 against the San Francisco Giants. His inaugural taste of the majors was predictably turbulent. Across 14 games (13 starts) for Colorado, Hughes posted a 6.33 ERA and an 0-8 record. On paper, those surface-level traditional figures look grim. However, a closer look under the hood reveals a far more nuanced picture of a young arm navigating his initial trial by fire. Triple-A momentum After a solid, albeit limited, spring training audition, Hughes was sent to Triple-A Albuquerque to start the 2026 campaign. He got off to a rough start, posting an 8.64 ERA in 25 innings across six starts. The strikeouts weren’t an issue as he had 32 against just six walks, but he was giving up a lot of contact and getting hit hard. At the end of April, he was placed on the injured list and missed most of May. After a pair of strong rehab starts with High-A Spokane, Hughes was sent back to the Isotopes where he looked like a man possessed. Over his next three starts in June, Hughes allowed just four hits across 15.2 innings with 16 strikeouts and five walks, limiting opponents to a .080/.179/.100 slash. His best outing of the year at any level came on June 25 when he fired six shutout innings at home against the Salt Lake Bees, giving up just two hits while striking out six. It was hard to ignore that Hughes had tapped into something while recovering from injury, and he had suddenly tamed the Pacific Coast League. item.title: Who is more to blame, the Cowboys offense or the defense?
item.description: Mandatory Credit: Kevin Jairaj-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Welcome to SB Nation Reacts, a survey of fans across the NFL. Throughout the year we ask questions of the most plugged-in Cowboys fans and fans across the country. This week, we wanted to know which side of the ball you are blaming more for the absolutely crushing loss against the Arizona Cardinals. We’ll make a case for and against each unit and then we’ll hit the polls for a vote. For blaming the offense: The Dallas Cowboys came into the season knowing the offense needed to carry the team. The defense was the defense, so the offense had to be elite. Remember GOTI? More like goat, and not the good kind. The offense has so many chances to put the game away but they couldn’t do it. Having CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens on the sidelines during crucial plays is never a good look. Wasted points allowed the Cardinals to hang around. Against blaming the offense: They scored 30 points. In the NFL, that is usually a winning number. They handed the defense a 14-point lead early in the fourth quarter, and a 10-point lead late in the fourth quarter. It’s hard to ask for more than that from an NFL offense. They may not have played great, but they provided margins in the fourth quarter anyone would have taken before the game. For blaming the defense: It’s hard to comprehend the collapse of the Cowboys defense the minute Gardner Minshew stepped onto the field. He and Tyler Allgeier shredded the defense in a way that is mathematically improbable. They gave up 27 points in a 16.5-minute stretch to end regulation. Absurd. Against blaming the defense: We know the Cowboys defense is bad, but the Cowboys offense and coaching kept making decisions like they’re good. Instead of running up the score early when the defense was balling, they only put up 14 points in the first half. The offense kept the Cardinals in the game in the second half with conservative decisions. And at least the defense was playing against Minshew/Allgeier, a combo they hadn’t prepared for. The offense doesn’t have that excuse. Hit the polls below and then tell us your thoughts in the comments. Who is to blame for the loss? Are you confident in the Cowboys? item.title: Liverpool v Arsenal: Two Penalties, But What About the Red Cards? – Opinion
item.description: Liverpool v Arsenal: Two Penalties, But What About the Red Cards? – Opinion Ankle Breakers, Head Slapping, and All the Media Want to Concentrate On Is a Non-Contact Headbutt, the Dive That Followed and Two Shirt Pulls!! Yes, it’s happening again, an over-the-top reaction to what The Arsenal did during the game with Liverpool. Let’s make it very clear that I agree the referee and VAR officials should have awarded a penalty, and they also missed another possible spot kick involving Tzolis. But here’s where I find the coverage of the game so one-sided and biased. If the penalties had been given, no player would have been under the threat of a long-term injury or sent off for violent conduct, resulting in a minimum three-match ban, unlike the laughable reaction to a “headbutt” that would also have resulted in a three-match violent conduct ban!! Both Arsenal players could have been booked, but that would have been the maximum possible outcome regarding the penalties. What About the Challenges on Odegaard? However, the second-minute tackle on Odegaard was one that could be seen as a career-threatening injury, and yet no action was taken, as happened when the same player should have received another yellow card just ten minutes later. Which of these four incidents should have been called out and covered by the media, simply because of the violence shown and the long-term consequences? Then we have the farce of Odegaard yet again being targeted for physical assault, when he was slapped around the head after being fouled once again by a player who then decided to fake a headbutt in order to get another player sent off. Why are these incidents not being reported and investigated with the same scrutiny that an obvious shirt pull has been? Where Is the Balance in the Media Coverage? I feel that all four incidents should have involved the VAR officials, and Liverpool should have had two penalties awarded regarding two of them. However, Liverpool should have been down to ten men as early as the second minute, if not by the fifteenth minute, while ending the game with nine men!! Slapping someone around the head is violent conduct and a red card, while faking a headbutt should be a yellow card. So let’s get these four incidents into perspective and rise above the usual media-biased hype against our club. By the way, although the officials had a bad day at the office, at least they didn’t favour either team. That’s not something that can be said about the media and pundits following Arsenal’s victory at Anfield . Do you agree with my views? Join the conversation in the comments below. item.title: Diamondbacks Need More Luck
item.description: Inspiration. In the last three seasons, the Diamondbacks failed to make the playoffs. They failed with 89 wins, they failed with 80 wins, and they failed with 86 wins. They were so very close. Why did they fall short? Every day, Torey Lovullo thinks about possible ways to improve the Diamondbacks. Many players strive to stack one percent improvements. And yet it wasn’t enough. Why? First Thoughts. One thought is that people more often find what they look for than what they are not looking for. The Diamondbacks are looking for improvements. Is it that simple? No. Another thought is that being optimistic helps people focus on good outcomes instead of bad outcomes. Perhaps focusing on good outcomes makes them more likely. Is it that simple? Although that is part of the answer, no. Perhaps the Diamondbacks need more luck. Luck has long been seen as significant. “Again I saw that under the sun the race is not to the swift, nor the battle to the strong, nor bread to the wise, nor riches to the intelligent, nor favor to the men of skill; but time and chance happen to them all.” — Ecclesiastes 9:11 What is luck? Luck is when the underdog Diamondbacks win games against strong teams, especially when the reasons are a combination of small things that are not apparent beforehand. One example was that in July the Diamondbacks swept the Dodgers in a three game series. Recently underdog wins happened many times each season! What specifically can the Diamondbacks do to make more good luck happen? One approach is flexibility to try different things, with recognition to quickly know what is working, and continuing what works (at least until it doesn’t). This could be called trial and error. It would be very lucky if this approach got the Diamondbacks to the playoffs. A better approach is to search for improvement ideas, implement some of the ideas, with recognition to quickly know whether each improvement is worth continuing, Instead of narrowly, search broadly for improvement ideas. This idea about improvements extends a previous idea about baseball players that I found years ago. On the baseball field, the best baseball players have a narrow focus on their tasks AND a broad focus on everything relevant that could impact their task. Instead of only a group of insiders, also talk with trusted outsiders who are wise and tell them what you are searching for. Keep searching for improvement ideas. If one idea turns out to be spectacularly great, don’t let it stop the search. If one idea fails, don’t let it stop the search. The best improvements to implement have small downsides, so that you can survive one or two failures. Although the upsides may be small, the improvement process can continue despite failures. Some improvements give the player (or the team) choices that can address situations that can occur in specific games, even if the situations are relatively rare. Some improvements make players on the other team react. Their failure to react would be to the Diam

item.title: Ollie Engen's performance a bright spot in UAlbany men's basketball's season opener
item.description: UAlbany's Ollie Engen looks to pass during a Monday, Nov. 2 game against Rhode Island College at Broadview Center in Albany. (Provided by UAlbany Athletics) ALBANY - Ollie Engen had no problem getting to the rim or pulling up for floaters in the paint early on in the University at Albany men's basketball season opener Monday night at Broadview Center. The junior guard just couldn't get those early looks to fall. So, after Engen missed his first four shots, coach Dwayne Killings took him out and gave him some advice. "Told him, ‘Just settle down,'" Killings said. "I thought he shorted two of his first shots. They were below the rim. I was just like, ‘finish higher above (the rim).'" Once Engen re-entered the game, he looked far more like the high-scoring player who was a U Sports second-team All-Canadian player last season at Queen's University in Ontario. He made 12 of his final 17 shots en route to a 25-point outing as he provided one of the bright spots in a 74-67 win over Division III Rhode Island College that was too close for comfort for Killings, Engen and the rest of the Great Danes. Engen, the Great Danes' 6-foot-5 point guard, also had six assists and grabbed five rebounds. He played a big part in UAlbany cruising to a 28-point lead with 13:11 left in the second half, but also took responsibility for many of the offensive struggles and defensive errors down the stretch that allowed the Anchormen to make what had looked to be a runaway UAlbany win into a far closer game than anticipated. UAlbany's Ollie Engen looks to pass during a Monday, Nov. 2 game against Rhode Island College at Broadview Center in Albany. (Provided by UAlbany Athletics) RIC outscored UAlbany 36-15 over the game's final 13 minutes. "Things are going to happen," Engen said. "You've got to be able to sustain that effort (on defense) for the full 30 seconds." Overall, Killings came away impressed with what Engen showed in his first U.S. college basketball game. "Ollie's got great pace, got great size, gets in the lane, knows how to pass," Killings said. "I think he showed just a small glimpse of what he's capable of." Jones flashes potential Freshman guard Tyler Jones came to UAlbany as the highest-rated high school recruit that Killings has brought into the program. When he stepped on the floor as one of the first two players off the bench, he immediately lived up to that hype. The 6-foot-3 Jones flashed his confidence, athleticism, defensive intensity and crafty ability to get to the basket in a 16-point performance. He shot 6-of-11 from the field, including 2-of-4 from 3-point range. "He's a confident player," Killings said. "He's not bashful by any means." UAlbany's Tyler Jones plays defense during a Monday, Nov. 2 game against Rhode Island College at Broadview Center in Albany. (Provided by UAlbany Athletics) There were some growing pains, too. item.title: How to the College Football Playoff first top-25 rankings on Tuesday night
item.description: Darian Mensah (10) and Malachi Toney (1) of the Miami Hurricanes run onto the field with their teammates before the game against the Pittsburgh Panthers at Hard Rock Stadium on Oct. 24, 2026 in Miami Gardens, Florida. (Michael Pimentel/ISI Photos/ISI Photos via Getty Images) The College Football Playoff selection committee will reveal the first of six rankings before Selection Sunday in December . Twelve teams are going to be in the field this year and it could be difficult to select who could make it into the bracket. Multiple blue bloods and powerhouse teams have lost multiple games. The committee is made up of 13 members who will use the past two months of football games to determine who is worthy of fighting for a national championship. Miami, which is undefeated, is expected to be at the top of the rankings and earn one of four first-round byes. However, the rest of the field is up for grabs and that could include Texas football who missed the CFP entirely in 2025. Alabama made the 12-team bracket last year even with three losses, giving hope to an SEC in which all but two teams have more than one conference loss. Texas Longhorns head coach Steve Sarkisian walks the sideline during the game against Mississippi State at Darrell K Royal–Texas Memorial Stadium on Saturday, Oct. 31, 2026 in Austin. (Aaron E. Martinez/Austin American-Statesman) GOLDEN: Will Texas make the CFP? Here's my first College Football Playoff field rankings Years of College Football Playoff runs decorate the walls as Texas Athletics celebrates the official grand opening of the new Frank and Wofford Denius Texas Football Training Complex, Sept. 4, 2026. (Sara Diggins/Austin American-Statesman) MORE CEDRIC GOLDEN: What are the Texas Longhorns saying about the first CFP reveal? Mum's the word Here is how to watch the first CFB bracket reveal: When is the CFP ranking show? What : College Football Playoff ranking show When : 6 p.m. CT Nov. 3 TV: ESPN How does the College Football Playoff work? The 12 teams that make of the CFP bracket are five automatic bids and seven at-large bids. Four of the automatic bids will go to the champions from the Power Four conferences (SEC, Big Ten, Big 12 and ACC) while the fifth goes to the highest-ranked team from either the American, Conference USA, MAC, Mountain West, Pac-12 or Sun Belt conferences. The rest of the field is selected based on where they are in the selection committee rankings. Depending on where teams fall in the bracket, the higher seeded, at-large team will host a first round game. Texas hosted Clemson in its first round of the 2024 College Football Playoff. Winners form the first-round games will play the top four teams on New Year's Eve or Day in either the Orange Bowl, Sugar Bowl, Cotton Bowl and Rose Bowl. The winners of that round will play in the semifinals, Jan. 14-15, in the Fiesta Bowl and Peach Bowl. When is the national title game? The national championship game will be Jan. 25, 2027 at Allegiant Stadium in Las V

item.title: Wolverines in the NFL: Blake Corum scores again, Josh Metellus makes 13 tackles
item.description: INGLEWOOD, CALIFORNIA - NOVEMBER 1: Blake Corum #24 of the Los Angeles Rams carries the ball during the third quarter of an NFL football game against the Los Angeles Chargers at SoFi Stadium on November 1, 2026 in Inglewood, California. (Photo by Brooke Sutton/Getty Images) | Getty Images Blake Corum scored for the second straight week, and two other former Michigan Wolverines helped the Rams keep the Chargers out of the end zone. Six Michigan alumni took the field at Ford Field as the Lions handed the Vikings their first loss of the season. And on Monday night, two former Michigan tight ends faced off in Seattle. Here’s how the Wolverines fared in Week 8 of the 2026 NFL season. Blake Corum gets the Rams’ ground game going The Rams had just 10 rushing yards at halftime against the Chargers. Corum more than doubled that on one play in the third quarter, breaking free for a 23-yard touchdown that turned a one-point lead into a 17-9 advantage. He finished with a team-high 73 yards on 11 carries, averaging 6.6 yards per attempt in the 24-9 win. Blake Corum with the smooth move and TD! LACvsLAR on FOX/FOX One Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/YP3lqMMQYg — NFL (@NFL) November 1, 2026 The Rams had two more former Wolverines making plays on defense. Edge rusher Josaiah Stewart finished with six tackles and a sack, while cornerback Josh Wallace made four tackles, including three solo stops. Josh Metellus makes 13 tackles as Detroit hands Minnesota its first loss Metellus finished with 13 tackles and a pass breakup in Minnesota’s 19-15 loss at Ford Field. On the other side, Aidan Hutchinson made four solo tackles and forced a fumble. He played 50 of Detroit’s 53 defensive snaps, as the Lions held Minnesota to 266 total yards. Rookies Derrick Moore and Jimmy Rolder also saw time on defense and special teams. Moore played 22 defensive snaps, and Rolder played 17 on defense and another 13 on special teams. Unfortunately, Rolder will miss the rest of the season due to a hamstring injury he suffered in this game. For Minnesota, fullback Max Bredeson played seven offensive snaps, and guard Trevor Keegan appeared off the bench. Colston Loveland leads Chicago in catches on Monday night Loveland caught 7-of-9 targets for 65 yards against Seattle on Monday Night Football. He led the Bears in receptions and finished second in receiving yards. On the other sideline, Seattle tight end AJ Barner turned his lone catch into a 17-yard gain on three targets. Former Michigan linebacker Devin Bush also saw action for Chicago. DJ Turner II recovers two fumbles in Bengals’ overtime win Turner recovered two fumbles and made three tackles as Cincinnati beat Tennessee, 43-36, in overtime. Unfortunately, Turner left the game in the fourth quarter due to injury, so hopefully he isn’t out for long. Insane play from DJ Turner to force a fumble on this screen pic.twitter.com/8qTOQE6VJt — mike (@bengals_sans) November 2, 2026 Fellow Bengals cornerback Daxton Hill made four solo tackles

item.title: Syracuse women’s basketball: our 26-27 season predictions
item.description: STORRS, CONNECTICUT - MARCH 23: The Syracuse Orange huddle up during the first half in the second round of the 2026 NCAA Women's Basketball Tournament against the Connecticut Huskies at Harry A. Gampel Pavilion on March 23, 2026 in Storrs, Connecticut. (Photo by Joe Buglewicz/Getty Images) | Getty Images Felisha Legette-Jack’s squad begins their season tonight at home against Sacred Heart. The TNIAAM staff goes over their overall record prediction, their conference record prediction, and postseason aspirations: Kevin 19-10, 11-7 NCAA 2nd Round It feels like this Syracuse team is also going to lean on their defense this season. The difference for the women is they have an All-ACC player in Uche Izoje to lean on. Izoje’s impact in the middle for the Orange should allow more space for the perimeter players and if the transfer guards can play like they showed in the UConn exhibition, I expect this team to be back in the NCAA Tournament. Dom: 20-9, 10-8, NCAA 1st Round Playbook for the Orange in 2026-27: there’s a solid chance Syracuse could leave the non-con schedule at 9-2 or 10-1 (my prediction has the latter, with the lone loss to Oklahoma). Think the losses start to pile up way more in a usually deep ACC, but Syracuse takes care of business against the programs it needs to beat and picks up a couple bubble wins but doesn’t get much in the Q1 win column. That said, it’s enough to get ‘Cuse as one of the final teams in the field. If healthy and avoiding foul trouble, Izoje provides a guaranteed floor of at least a .500 team. If some and not all of the other major offseason additions work out, that pushes the Orange into 18-21-win territory. Sam: 19-10, 10-8, NCAA First Round I like this group more than I like the men’s team – granted, I know much more about MBB than WBB – but I just don’t think there’s a proportional amount of wins on the schedule, especially in ACC play, to reflect that. 3-point shooting will likely be a weakness, but in women’s basketball, it’s easier to live with that since percentages around the country are worse and the shot is not quite as efficient. It’s why the mid-range game is still so prevalent, and bigs like Uche Izoje are encouraged to take mid-range shots. What SU did do is commit to an identity. An identity of being dominant on the inside on both ends. Izoje, Jaleesa Molina, and Sarah Rambus will control the glass on most nights. They could play huge lineups with Emely Rodriguez at the 2. Tyi Skinner will give them just enough shooting and shot creation out of the point guard spot as well. Regardless, I still think there’s a chasm between SU and the top teams in the sport. Audrey: 18-11, 9-9, NCAA First Round I would feel much more confident about this group if they’d been together last year. On paper, this group seems like they ought to command the paint on both ends of the floor. item.title: Miami Dolphins: Deux et Machina, not for us!
item.description: MIAMI GARDENS, FLORIDA - NOVEMBER 01: DeMario Douglas #3 of the New England Patriots carries the ball for a touchdown against Juju Brents #8 of the Miami Dolphins during the fourth quarter of the game at Hard Rock Stadium on November 01, 2026 in Miami Gardens, Florida. (Photo by Megan Briggs/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Truths: The Miami Dolphins have played two “one-half” games the last two weeks. A “half-game” was good enough against the hapless New York Jets but a “half-game” was NOWHERE near good enough against the unspectacular New England Patriots. How they reached the Super Bowl last year just shows that lady luck and buffoonery still reign supreme in the NFL. Zebras gone wild – Courtesy of Greek and Latin writer s: And let us not forget how the Patriots are the recipient of every close call, especially against us. I literally think that on EVERY single non-procedural penalty, the refs call up to Goodell and Satan to ask permission to charge the Patriots with a penalty. I am not joking. A bunch of blind shamans from Mongolia would do a better job officiating. How in the name of God do the field refs rule the NE dude short and then go to commercial and then when we get back from the commercial we have a “Deux et Machina” moment where NE is GIVEN a first down AND Steve Ross is kicked in the groin to boot. For those of you who may not know “Deux et Machina” ….it is a Latin phrase written into plays/stories thousands of years ago to explain how a character can be in the Aegean Sea one moment and the very next scene the character is sitting on top of Mount Vesuvius. The term translates to God and Machine. It takes God and Machine to stop the Miami Dolphins. And the networks and the NFL trot out Gene Steratore (remember he is the Phins major Zerba enemy) to say how stupid Dolphins’ fans are for even questioning the infinite wisdom of the NFL. In the offseason, I will rack my own brain and re-watch games where the Fins were completely ruined by the refs. I will try to write a treatise on this. I HATE having to sound whiny about the officiating, but IT IS A NATIONWIDE STORY. Armando Salguero et al have discussed the garbage that masquerades as officiating. Like D’Attaglia in the Godfather , NE is not our real enemy; just an annoyance. Buffalo is our Barzini! On to the game itself: NE is NOT very much better than us. Don’t forget that. The announcers were fawning over the overrated Drake Maye. He isn’t that good. He throws a decent long ball but remember NE got the matchups they wanted. Not hard throws. He isn’t 1/100 th the QB that Tom Brady was. Know this: it is 10,000 times harder to thread a 3 rd and 18-yard deep-square-in under a withering pass rush (one of the routes that put Aikman and Irvin in the HOF) versus throwing a deep ball when he has 5 seconds to throw with very little pressure. item.title: Dimorphos in sight: Europe's Hera probe gets its 1st look at battered space rock (photo)
item.description: null Europe's Hera planetary defense spacecraft is closing in on the binary asteroid system targeted by NASA's DART deflection test, and can now tell the two rocky bodies apart. Hera is nearing the end of its voyage to the Didymos asteroid system, having launched on a SpaceX Falcon 9 rocket in October 2024. The spacecraft snapped the image of Didymos and the smaller Dimorphos on Oct. 18 from a distance of 795 miles (1280 kilometers) from the pair, which are currently about 122 million miles (197 million km) from Earth. "With this image, the smaller Dimorphos asteroid becomes visible for the first time," Michael Kueppers, Hera project scientist at the European Space Agency (ESA), said in a statement . "Before this acquisition, the spacecraft was still resolving the Didymos system as a single dot. But now, even though Dimorphos is made up of only around one pixel in this initial image, it is clearly well separated from its parent body." The Double Asteroid Redirection Test (DART) smashed into Dimorphos in September 2022, changing the asteroid's orbit in a pioneering planetary defense demonstration. Hera's job is to survey the damage and refine our understanding of the impact, as well as the asteroids themselves. Hera performed braking maneuvers earlier in October to slow its approach and put it on course to rendezvous with the binary system. The spacecraft is designed to make follow-up observations of the asteroids using 12 payloads, providing new insights that will prove valuable for planetary defense efforts. The mission also carries a pair of cubesats for a closer look and eventual landing on the 495-foot-wide (151 meters) Dimorphos. A series of images captured by the DART spacecraft as it sped to impact the asteroid Dimorphos on Sept. 26, 2022. (Image credit: NASA/JHUAPL) For now, Hera is continuing its approach and preparing for arrival, with a big reveal expected to occur later this month. "Our views will grow much sharper as Hera comes closer," said ESA's mission manager Ian Carnelli. "We will unveil the first detailed images of Dimorphos — the first object in the solar system to have had its orbit measurably shifted by human action — on 25 November."

item.title: Dad texted daughter 'go easy' before NYC Marathon runner’s death
item.description: Rachel Apa, 24, was about seven miles into the New York City Marathon on Nov. 1 when she texted her father for the first time on the course. "She said, 'Never felt better. I must have done the carb loading correctly for the first time,'" her father, Steve Apa, said. But 17 miles later – just two from the finish line – Rachel Apa collapsed. She was pronounced dead hours later. Steve Apa said his daughter was diagnosed with rhabdomyolysis , a rare injury that causes muscle breakdown and is usually caused by overexertion, according to the Cleveland Clinic. The New York Police Department confirmed to USA TODAY that a 24-year-old female experienced a "medical episode" near mile marker 24 and was transported to the hospital in critical condition. The marathon was Rachel Apa's first. She ran it for the Parkinson's Foundation after her paternal grandfather died from the disease. "My grandfather was my role model growing up. He taught me to stay active, push my limits, and embrace challenges, shaping my love for sports and movement," she wrote on a fundraising page. New York Road Runners, which organizes the race, said in a statement: "We are deeply saddened by Rachel’s passing following running in Sunday’s race. Our thoughts and sincere sympathies are with her family, friends, and the entire running community." More: What running does for your body Rachel Apa was a lifelong athlete, father says Rachel Apa, a native of Lewisberry, Pennsylvania, was a lifelong athlete and former field hockey player at Bucknell University, her father said. "She did everything she's supposed to for the training up to the marathon," Steve Apa said. "I remember her telling me, 'Dad, this weekend's my 18-mile run.' So she was fully trained, fully prepared." While Steve Apa was at home in Pennsylvania tracking his daughter on the marathon app, his wife, Michelle Apa, was along the route. He was texting her throughout the race. "I said, 'This is your first marathon. Go easy. Don't go out too fast,'" he said. "And then, every mile, I would just text her the mile number." Around mile 18, she texted him, "Ugh" and then "Ow," he said. "I said, 'go easy,' and then I pinged her when she hit the 20th mile and she said, 'ow,'" Steve Apa said. That was the last time he heard from her. At mile 23, Steve Apa sent his daughter another text: "Final stretch. Finished, not speed." Michelle Apa was waiting for her daughter around mile 25 when they noticed she appeared to have stopped moving on the tracking app. When she headed to mile 24, spectators told her an ambulance had just taken Rachel Apa to the hospital. A spectator later told Steve and Michelle Apa that they saw Rachel collapse and immediately began giving her CPR before eventually trying a defibrillator. She was then taken by ambulance to Mount Sinai Hospital where doctors worked on her from about 2 to 9 p.m. local time, Steve Apa said. item.title: King's Academy volleyball advances to first state final since 2007
item.description: King's Academy volleyball is headed to its first state championship match since 2007. The Lions swept Pensacola Catholic (25-23, 25-20, 25-20) to advance to the Class 3A state final at Polk State College in Winter Haven, Florida. "We're pumped," said King's Academy head coach Bethany Avila. "We've been working toward this all year long, just tried to stay humble and take one game at a time and work really hard in practice." The game was a straight sweep, but it was not without its challanges. Though King's Academy looked dominant for most of the first set, the No. 2 seed Lions had to survive a late 7-1 run by Pensacola Catholic and then revisit the court after a match point was overturned before finally putting away the Crusaders for the early match lead. Pensacola Catholic didn't make things much easier as the morning went on. The Crusaders were forced into an early timeout in the second set after King's Academy seized momentum, but they recovered with their own run and would tie the set at 11-11. But the Lions were able to overcome challenges the rest of the way, thanks in large part to their dominant presence in the middle. With 54 blocks heading into the state semifinal, freshman Yasmin Nunes shined on the biggest stage with her presence in the middle. So, too, did junior newcomer Anabelle Bencosme on the outside. "They both fly under the radar because they're new," Avila said. "They're kind of our secret weapons, but they're not so secret anymore. They have super high verticals that they've been working on this year and that is what has elevated their game both literally and figuratively." Between Nunes and Jordan Molnar, King's Academy was ready for almost every play at the net. and Molnar, who is King's Academy's setter, does just about everything well. "Jordan Molnar was on fire as far as her blocking," Avila said. "I know she is our setter, but she is also our top blocker and she shut down their outside, and she stepped in and blocked their middles, too. She just knows how to get a point." King's Academy has won three state championships, but the most recent came in 2006, 20 years ago. The Lions are ready to end that drought, but to do so, they will have to face off against the winner of No. 1 Merritt Island and No. 4 Pine Crest, who began their state semifinal at 1 p.m. Alex Peterman is a high school sports reporter for The Palm Beach Post. He can be reached at apeterman@usatodayco.com This article originally appeared on Palm Beach Post: King's Academy volleyball advances to first state final since 2007

item.title: Pat Murphy gets brutally honest on Brewers’ World Series parade
item.description: Matt Marton-Imagn Images Pat Murphy gets brutally honest on Brewers’ World Series parade appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Milwaukee Brewers have been celebrating their World Series championship over the past week. The team went to Thursday night’s Green Bay Packers’ game, they’ve been on various shows such as Saturday Night Live , and the Brewers participated in a World Series parade on Friday. Manager Pat Murphy reflected on the championship parade during a Tuesday appearance on MLB Network. “It blew me away,” Murphy said. “… 700,000 people they said. They were just there to support the Brewers, and how happy, bringing everybody together. And seeing the joy that it spread what our guys did to win that championship. That just did so much for our community, for our state. “Yeah, you felt it, you felt it at that parade. Amazing turnout.” Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) The championship represented the first World Series victory in Brewers’ franchise history. Their only other Fall Classic appearance came in 1982, when they were defeated by the St. Louis Cardinals. Brewers fans have been waiting for this moment for a long time to say the least. The city of Milwaukee provided an energetic atmosphere during Friday’s World Series parade as fans celebrated with the players. The Brewers’ next goal will be to develop a dynasty. Milwaukee features a number of players under contract for years to come. It wouldn’t be surprising to see this ball club reach the Fall Classic once again sooner rather than later. In fact, it would be surprising if they failed to seriously contend over the next few years. For now, however, the team has earned the right to celebrate their 2026 World Series win. item.title: Fashola urges grassroots mobilisation ahead of 2027 polls
item.description: By Olasunkanmi Akoni Former Lagos State Governor and Minister of Works, Babatunde Fashola, has urged All Progressives Congress (APC) leaders in the South-West to strengthen grassroots mobilisation and engage stakeholders across party lines to secure victory in the 2027 general elections. Fashola made the call on Tuesday at a strategic meeting of South-West political stakeholders held in Ikeja, Lagos. The meeting was attended by Lagos State Governor Babajide Sanwo-Olu, his deputy, Dr Obafemi Hamzat, APC State Chairman, Pastor Cornelius Ojelabi, and other party leaders and zonal coordinators. Fashola outlined a strategy for unifying party structures and increasing voter turnout ahead of the elections. He urged participants from the six states in the zone to establish structured stakeholder engagement forums at three levels: state, local government and ward. Emphasising the need for inclusive engagement, he said stakeholders should not be limited to APC members but should include individuals and groups capable of influencing electoral outcomes across party lines. “A stakeholder is anyone who can impact election outcomes, spanning party lines, opposing caucuses, artisans and union members,” he said. Fashola, who is working with former Ondo State Governor Segun Mimiko, former Ekiti State Governor Segun Oni and Secretary Senator Fatai Buhari on the Presidential Campaign Council’s South-West strategy, said he would visit each state after the initial engagement forums had been established. He said the visits would provide opportunities to address local political concerns, respect the peculiarities of each state and escalate issues requiring national intervention. Describing politics as local, Fashola urged party leaders to reach out to newly registered voters and re-engage those who had become apathetic towards the electoral process. He also called on them to recognise the significance of the country’s North-South political rotation and take advantage of the prevailing political moment to strengthen the party’s electoral prospects. The meeting later went into a closed-door session, with a communiqué expected at the end of the deliberations for release to the media. The post Fashola urges grassroots mobilisation ahead of 2027 polls appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Confirmed: Barcelona starting lineup to face Aston Villa
item.description: Confirmed: Barcelona starting lineup to face Aston Villa FC Barcelona will be looking to regain some momentum in the UEFA Champions League as they take on Aston Villa at Camp Nou this evening. Heading into this game, Barcelona have officially announced their starting eleven that will take on the Premier League outfit, with Hansi Flick making minimal changes from the side that secured a 6-1 win over Deportivo Alaves on the weekend. Brian Farinas continues at right-back after impressing against Alaves. He started in the absence of several key defenders including Eric Garcia, Jules Kounde and Xavi Espart. Joao Cancelo continues on the opposite flank while Flick has made only change in defence, bringing in Gerard Martin at centre-back at the expense of Frenkie de Jong. Martin starts alongside Pau Cubarsi in central defence, with Joan Garcia starting in goal. In midfield, Flick has remained unchanged, with Pedri and Rodri forming the double-pivot, with additional support from Fermin Lopez. Fermin was outstanding against Alaves and he will hope to continue the same form against Aston Villa this evening, especially with Dani Olmo currently sidelined with an injury. There is one change in attack. Karim Adeyemi makes way for Anthony Gordon, who scored in the 6-1 win over Alaves. Gordon forms the familiar Barcelona frontline alongside Lamine Yamal and Raphinha, both of who scored a brace in the last game.

item.title: How Colts can control NFL trade deadline with Jonathan Taylor sweepstakes
item.description: How Colts can control NFL trade deadline with Jonathan Taylor sweepstakes originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Indianapolis Colts are trade deadline sellers, having already shipped out Quenton Nelson to the Seattle Seahawks and DeForest Buckner to the San Francisco 49ers . But their biggest piece has yet to move. Running back Jonathan Taylor is garnering serious trade interest from teams around the NFL, and he might be the top trade target for this year's deadline. That has given the Colts a very unique opportunity. As ESPN's Ben Solak highlighted, the Colts can control the trade deadline with the sweepstakes for Taylor. As plenty of top contenders try for Taylor, the Colts' control of the biggest trade chip gives them the key to the trade deadline this year. How the Colts can control the NFL trade deadline with Jonathan Taylor "But the market is paralyzed by Taylor, as all these teams stare down the Colts and their towering demands," Solak writes. While he believes some team might pivot from Taylor and go after someone like Tony Pollard, considering the interested teams in Taylor are top contenders competing with one another, not landing Taylor would be doubly bad for a lot of teams. The Denver Broncos , Seattle Seahawks, Green Bay Packers , New York Giants , Minnesota Vikings , and Cincinnati Bengals are the teams most commonly linked to Taylor this season. With so many interested teams for a Taylor trade, the trade deadline market might not get rolling until the Colts make a final decision on Taylor. MORE : NFL insiders reveal four landing spots for Colts ’ Jonathan Taylor They could decide to keep him, taking him off the block, or they could trade him away. Either way, until a decision is made on Taylor, his status as a trade candidate could stop some of those contenders from making moves for help at this year's deadline. While a team or two might pivot to other positional needs, all of the RB-needy teams will have their deadlines determined by the Colts and their willingness to part with Taylor. It's a unique opportunity for the Colts, as the trade deadline might only move along based on what they do with Taylor. Indianapolis can also determine the wide receiver trade market with Josh Downs, so the Colts really have the means to control the trade deadline this year. As Solak put it, the Colts can "paralyze" the NFL trade market this November with the sweepstakes for Taylor. Whether they trade or not is still up in the air. But the Colts should be able to control the deadline this season, all thanks to the Taylor sweepstakes. item.title: NYC Marathon Runner Rachel Apa, 24, Dies Just 2 Miles From Finish Line During First Race
item.description: Bucknell University Rachel Apa had a special reason for taking on the New York City Marathon. The 24-year-old was running in honor of her late grandfather, who passed away from Parkinson’s disease. Tragically, Apa never made it to the finish line as she collapsed and died. Apa collapsed near Mile 24 of Sunday’s race, just two short miles from the finish line in Central Park. This was her first marathon, and she was participating as part of the Parkinson’s Champions team to raise money for research, according to The New York Times . Her family was cheering her on along the sidelines as she made her way through the marathon. Her mother, Michelle, was following along in person, while her father, Steve, tracked her progress from home. The race appeared to be going well, as Apa reportedly told her father early in the race that she had never felt better. However, her messages became more concerning as she complained of pain. She eventually sent a message saying she was in the final stretch, just before collapsing. A bystander began to perform CPR as soon as they noticed Apa, and then medical personnel took over. Medical staff continued lifesaving efforts and used an automated external defibrillator before EMS arrived. EMS transported Apa to Mount Sinai Medical Center, but despite their best efforts, she died later that evening in the hospital. Apa was a former Division I field hockey player at Bucknell University. Her father, Steve, described her as being in excellent health and stated that she had trained and prepared for this marathon. Her father also told The New York Times that he believed his daughter died from rhabdomyolysis, a potentially life-threatening condition that involved the breakdown of muscle tissue. However, the NYC medical examiner said that the cause of death has yet to be determined. In a statement from New York Road Runners, which organized this marathon, they stated that they were deeply saddened by Apa’s passing and extended their condolences to her family, friends, and the running community. item.title: What will Houston Texans do at NFL trade deadline? Decision is more complex than it seems.
item.description: Texans general manager Nick Caserio faces a consequential decision at next Tuesday's NFL trade deadline. (Melissa Phillip/Houston Chronicle) It happens every year. The NFL's trade deadline comes around and teams are forced to confront a major question at the midpoint of their season. Do they sacrifice the future for immediate help in hopes of competing for a Super Bowl? Do they start over and sell off assets as they plan for the future? Or do they stay put? That's where the Houston Texans sit one week before the Nov. 10 trade deadline as general manager Nick Caserio confronts those questions. Since coach DeMeco Ryans arrived nearly four years ago, Caserio and the Texans have taken a measured approach to the trade deadline. They haven't quite been buyers and they definitely haven't been sellers. They've mostly stayed quiet during this crucial part of the season, though it hasn't always been for a lack of trying. Last season, the Texans called the Jets about running back Breece Hall , but felt the asking price - a third-round pick - was too high. This year will more than likely be more of the same. Texans Insider with Jonathan M. Alexander Sign up for an in-depth newsletter with Houston Texans news, features and predictions. The Texans are 2-5 heading into their Week 9 game against the Los Angeles Chargers on Sunday. There are certainly areas the Texans could upgrade that could help improve their chance at making the playoffs. But their five losses in seven games make it a complex decision. The Texans aren't quite bad enough this year to start selling assets, but they also aren't good enough to become buyers, either. Three more losses would almost surely knock them out of the playoffs. Two losses would put them on the brink. And the more losses the Texans have, the more valuable their draft picks will become. Caserio said at his off-week press conference that they would be open to a deal - whatever that may look like. "If it makes sense, great," Caserio said. "If not, so… we've had conversations. We've talked to most of the league here." TEXANS AT CHARGERS When: 3:05 p.m. Sunday Where: SoFi Stadium; Inglewood, Calif. TV: CBS Radio: 95.7 FM, 610 AM, 101.1 FM (Spanish) Caserio already made a major move last month when he traded a second-round pick and a seventh for Marvin Harrison Jr. and a sixth-round pick, which was significant draft capital Houston relinquished. The Texans' current 2027 picks include a first-, a third-, a fourth-, two sixths and a seventh-round pick. "I don't think anybody's really worried about the draft right now," Caserio said when asked about the second-round pick. "There are a lot of ways that you can recoup picks at some point along the way, whether it's this year or whether it's in the offseason. Lionel Scaloni and Argentina are entering a new era of the national team's history as they get ready to meet Uruguay and Costa Rica in a pair of international friendlies this November. These two matches will be the first without retired legends Lionel Messi and Nicolas Otamendi, who made their farewell to international football last international break against Benin . Now, the Albiceleste will begin building towards the 2030 FIFA World Cup by moving forward without those two superstars, figuring out the impossible task of replacing them as best they can. Last international break, the Albiceleste beat Bolivia and Burkina Faso by big margins without Messi, but his farewell against Benin was still on everyone's mind the whole way. Now, with his retirement in the rear view mirror, Scaloni will navigate friendlies against Uruguay and Costa Rica as the first true proving ground for players in the effort to move forward into the new era. MORE: Lionel Messi explains retirement from international duty Argentina roster for November friendlies vs. Uruguay, Costa Rica Argentina head coach Lionel Scaloni has called in 28 players for the two friendly matches in the November 2026 international break, with the squad revealed on Tuesday, November 3 . The Albiceleste will meet Uruguay first on Friday, November 13 at La Bombonera, before facing CONCACAF nation Costa Rica four days later on Tuesday, November 17 at Mario Kempes Stadium in Cordoba. item.title: Lions Coach Dan Campbell Says Linebacker Jack Campbell Is ‘Improving’ After Neck Injury
item.description: Dan Campbell; Jack Campbell Credit: Bryan M. Bennett/Getty; Michael Owens/Getty NEED TO KNOW Detroit Lions head coach Dan Campbell said linebacker Jack Campbell is “improving” after he suffered a serious neck injury on Nov. 1 “It’s not easy because he’s always going to be on our minds over here,” Dan said on 97.1 The Ticket Jack has remained hospitalized since the collision Detroit Lions head coach Dan Campbell provided an update on linebacker Jack Campbell’s condition after the Pro Bowler suffered a serious neck injury on Sunday, Nov. 1. During an interview with 97.1 The Ticket on Tuesday, Nov. 3, the Lions head coach said Jack, 26, is “improving” as he remains hospitalized. The team confirmed that the former first-round pick sustained a neck injury in the second half of the Lions’ 19-15 home win over the Minnesota Vikings on Sunday. “It’s not easy because he’s always going to be on our minds over here,” Dan, 50, told the radio show, adding, “The good news is he is improving.” Dan Campbell; Jack Campbell on Sunday, Nov. 1, 2026 Credit: Amy Lemus/NurPhoto via Getty; Jorge Lemus/NurPhoto via Getty Dan said “knowing he’s doing better,” in reference to Jack, and keeping the other Lions players informed on the positive updates “helps everybody just get a better handle on this.” The head coach added, “All we can do at this point is just continue to pray for Jack, put our thoughts on him when we have a minute, and on his family — and it’s working, like I said, because he’s improving.” Dan asked for continued prayers for Jack. “Please continue to do that. We’ll leave it at that, so continue to pray for him. But it is positive,” he told 97.1. Jack sustained the neck injury when his head collided with Vikings tight end T.J. Hockenson’s hip when he went to make a tackle in the fourth quarter. Jack landed face-first on the turf at Ford Field and remained motionless for several moments. Players from both teams took a knee and appeared emotional as medical staff tended to Jack, who was eventually placed on a stretcher and carted off the field. He has been hospitalized since the incident. Follow your favorite athletes on and off the field with PEOPLE’s free sports newsletter — sign up now! Dan told reporters in a press conference on Monday, Nov. 2 that he went to visit Jack and the linebacker’s “very positive” family. “I got to go see him last night, it was good, it was positive. Got to see his parents, talk to his wife and everybody’s in good spirits.” Read the original article on People

item.title: Braves Lock In Acuña And Albies At Shocking Bargain Prices
item.description: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect The biggest shock in Atlanta sports news isn’t a trade or a star leaving town. It is how little money the Atlanta Braves will pay their two best players next year. The team exercised their options for Ronald Acuña Jr and Ozzie Albies for the 2027 season, locking them in for a combined total of just $24 million. That figure is shockingly low for two players who have carried the franchise for a decade. Most fans expected a massive price tag for the 2023 NL MVP and the long-time second baseman. Instead, the club secured Acuña for $17 million and Albies for $7 million. This move was the “no-brainer decision of all no-brainer decisions” after the team won 94 games and claimed the NL East title, according to Battery Power . The organization also cleared the books by reinstating four pitchers from the injured list, including Spencer Strider and Hurston Waldrep, just as the postseason kicked off. The Price Tag Defies Logic It is rare to see a team keep its core stars for such a low cost in modern baseball. Acuña is set to make $6 million less than the standard MLB qualifying offer, which is a massive win for the front office. Some fans thought Acuña would not return, but those rumors ignored the reality of the contract signed years ago. The deal allows Atlanta to keep the player who achieved the historic 40-home run, 70-stolen base season in 2023. Ozzie Albies brings a similar value with his $7 million price tag for the upcoming year. While he had a career low in wRC+ this season, the team views him as a bridge for younger prospects waiting in Double-A. Replacing him would likely cause more trouble than simply keeping him on the roster for one more year. The financial flexibility this creates is huge for the rest of the roster. With $24 million committed to two All-Stars, the team has room to address other needs like shortstop. The Braves are looking at trade options such as Jeremy Peña from the Astros, as their current plans with Ha-Seong Kim did not work out. This budget allows them to be aggressive in the market while keeping their stars. Health Remains the Only Wild Card The only question left for both players is their physical status heading into next season. Acuña tore his ACL in 2024 but returned in 2025, proving he can still dominate when healthy. When he is not healthy, people hear about it constantly, but the team is betting on his recovery. The same logic applies to Albies, whose value skyrockets when he is on the field and playing his usual style. Reinstating the pitching staff shows the team is ready to move forward with a full squad. Neither Spencer Schwellenbach nor Spencer Strider should be anticipated to immediately resume their previous performance levels. Joey Wentz suffered a lower body injury blowing out his right ACL during a Spring Training bunt attempt. The front office knows these pitchers need time, but the moves made on Thursday signal a clear path forward. The focus now shifts to the trade mark

item.title: ‘Uncle Sam, Osoba, others built Daily Times, I’m just a custodian’ — Anosike
item.description: By Efe Onodjae The Chairman of Folio Media Group, owners of Daily Times of Nigeria, Fidelis Anosike, has described himself as a custodian of the newspaper, crediting its founding fathers and former leaders for building the institution into a major force in Nigeria’s history. Anosike spoke at the Daily Times Heroes Award in Lagos, where he said the newspaper’s legacy was built through the sacrifices and contributions of distinguished individuals, including Uncle Sam, Aremo Olusegun Osoba and Yemi Ogunbiyi. The event, themed ‘Honouring the Past, Shaping the Future’, brought together stakeholders to celebrate individuals who contributed to the growth and development of the newspaper. Anosike said Daily Times did not belong to him, stressing that his responsibility was to preserve its legacy and ensure its continued relevance. “When we talk about Daily Times, it doesn’t belong to me. Daily Times belongs to Uncle Sam, Osoba, Yemi Ogunbiyi, late Dele Cole and Chief Onyema Ugochukwu. They built Daily Times. “I’m just a custodian, and I’m one of the luckiest custodians you can ever find because all of them have rallied around us to make sure that we celebrate what we’re celebrating today and that we can actually shape the future,” he said. He noted that many of those who built the newspaper were in their 20s and 30s at the time, adding that their contributions extended beyond journalism to nation-building. Anosike also recalled that some former contributors and leaders of the newspaper went on to establish or strengthen other media organisations, citing Sam Amuka’s contribution to Vanguard. He said Daily Times played a significant role in shaping Nigeria’s national identity, arguing that its influence went beyond its status as a newspaper organisation. “Sometimes people think that Daily Times is a newspaper company. It started as a newspaper company, but Daily Times, the nation built it. Nigeria is not Nigeria today if there was no Daily Times,” he added. The post ‘Uncle Sam, Osoba, others built Daily Times, I’m just a custodian’ — Anosike appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Security agencies rescue eight kidnap victims in Kaduna
item.description: By Ibrahim Hassan-Wuyo KADUNA – Security agencies, comprising the Office of the National Security Adviser (ONSA), Department of State Services (DSS), Nigeria Police Force and the Military, have rescued eight kidnap victims during coordinated operations in Kaduna State. The victims were rescued between October 31 and November 2, 2026, in intelligence-driven operations conducted in the Millennium City and Marabar Rido areas of Chikun Local Government Area, in collaboration with the Kaduna State Government. Addressing journalists at the DSS Command headquarters in Kaduna, the Commissioner of Police, CP Muhammad Rabiu, said the operations were part of sustained efforts to identify, disrupt and dismantle criminal networks responsible for repeated kidnappings in the areas. He said the communities had witnessed recurring abductions, raising concerns among residents and attracting public attention to the security situation. The rescued victims were identified as Jamila Muhammad, 27, wife of Abdulkadir Bello; Talatu Yakubu, 40; Yunana Bawa, 30; Calista Bishop, 27; Chidinma Onuwere, 36; Eucharia Obi, 41; Godiya Victor, 50; and an eight-year-old girl, Miracle Alex. The latest rescue came barely three weeks after security operatives freed Ahmad Zakka and members of his family from captivity on October 15, 2026. Rabiu said the successive operations demonstrated the determination of security agencies to secure the release of abducted persons and dismantle criminal networks operating across the state. He acknowledged the coordination provided by ONSA, the operational support of the Police, the intelligence contributions of the DSS and the involvement of the Military. The police commissioner also commended the Kaduna State Government, under Governor Uba Sani, for its cooperation and support in tackling kidnapping and banditry. He said the operations were in line with President Bola Tinubu’s commitment to strengthening national security and protecting lives and property through improved collaboration among security and intelligence agencies. Rabiu disclosed that security agencies were intensifying operations across the state, with additional personnel and equipment, including 30 operational vans and eight armoured personnel carriers, to be deployed to strengthen security and improve response to criminal activities. He noted that criminal groups often exploited the difficult terrain in parts of Kaduna State to launch attacks and evade security operatives. The commissioner urged residents to support security agencies by providing credible and actionable intelligence on the identities, activities and movements of suspected kidnappers and other criminal elements. He assured the public that information supplied would be treated confidentially and acted upon appropriately. Rabiu also called on traditional rulers, community leaders and other stakeholders to support efforts to tackle insecurity. He urged media organisations to maintain responsible and professional report

item.title: Soludo approves remodelling of Upper Iweka
item.description: By Vincent Ujumadu AWKA – The Anambra State Executive Council has approved the remodelling of Upper Iweka, Onitsha, as part of the state government’s urban regeneration programme. The project is expected to transform the aesthetics, functionality and land use of the area, a major gateway into Anambra State. The Commissioner for Information and Value Reformation, Dr Law Mefor, disclosed this while briefing journalists after the weekly State Executive Council meeting at the Government House, Awka. He said the remodelling would cover parks and other public spaces, giving the area a new look in line with the state government’s vision of a livable and prosperous homeland. Mefor added that a detailed master plan and design for the project would be unveiled soon. At the meeting, the council also directed the Anambra Road Traffic Management Agency (ARTMA) to issue a one-month notice to owners of abandoned vehicles on roads across the state to remove them. The commissioner said vehicles not removed after the expiration of the notice would be impounded, taken away and scrapped by the government. He explained that the measure was intended to eliminate road hazards, improve traffic flow and enhance the safety and appearance of roads across the state. The council also approved the commencement of the selection, placement and training of the third batch of the One Youth, Two Skills entrepreneurship programme. Mefor said the Ministry of Youth Development would announce the eligibility requirements and application procedures in due course. He recalled that two batches of the programme had been completed, with more than 13,000 youths trained, empowered and mentored in over 60 skill areas. According to him, more than 5,000 beneficiaries have become millionaires and are now training and empowering other young people under the programme’s pay-it-forward model. “The One Youth, Two Skills initiative remains a flagship youth empowerment programme of the Soludo administration aimed at creating a new tribe of skilled, productive and self-reliant youths,” Mefor said. The post Soludo approves remodelling of Upper Iweka appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: N70,000 transport allowance saga: PENGASSAN begs Ajaero, Osifo to sheathe swords, unite Labour
item.description: …Says rift not good for collective interests of workers By Victor Ahiuma-Young & Omotola Aremo The Petroleum and Natural Gas Senior Staff Association of Nigeria, PENGASSAN, has called on the President of the Nigeria Labour Congress, NLC, Comrade Joe Ajaero, and his counterpart in the Trade Union Congress of Nigeria, TUC, Comrade Festus Osifo, to sheathe their swords and urgently resolve the differences between the two major labour centres in the interest of Nigerian workers. The appeal comes amid the lingering controversy between the NLC and TUC over the Federal Government’s proposed N70,000 transport allowance, which the TUC leadership rejected. The disagreement has exposed differences between the two labour central organisations over the handling of the allowance, raising concerns about the ability of organised labour to sustain a common front in its engagements with the Federal Government. Agoro warned that the divisions could weaken labour’s collective bargaining power and undermine its responsibility to defend workers’ interests. The PENGASSAN President, who made the appeal at the Labour Writers Association of Nigeria (LAWAN) conference in Lagos, urged both leaders to prioritise dialogue, reconciliation and cooperation, insisting that the interests of Nigerian workers must take precedence over institutional disagreements. Speaking in his personal capacity, while also representing Osifo at the event, Agoro challenged the two labour leaders to practise the unity they had encouraged other labour organisations to embrace, stressing that the time had come for them to resolve their differences and present a common front in engagements with the government. He said: “I listened carefully to Comrade Joe Ajaero, and I want him and his twin brother to do the same thing that he advised Labour Correspondents Association of Nigeria, LACAN, and LAWAN to do. “We cannot shy away from the fact that things are not the way they are supposed to be with the two of them. So, in the same manner that you have advised both LACAN and LAWAN to come together without having to dissolve their centres and go for retreat, I think it is time we tell the two of them to pull back a bit and talk to themselves. “The reason why we have this platform is because we are representing the people (workers), and the interest of the people must be number one on our minds. Anything we are doing that will jeopardise what the people have put us in this position to do, we must move away from it. “We don’t normally come with problems alone; we always like to prepare solutions. I think it is time for both TUC and NLC to sit down and have a Memorandum of Understanding on how we want this relationship to work. “The Federal Government of Nigeria has married two wives, and if they think they have anything to gain by the discord between both labour centres, I think they are just joking. item.title: Ejiro Amos Tafiri Unveils REVERIE, Its Spring/Summer 2027 Collection, Celebrating Reinvention in African Luxury
item.description: Ejiro Amos Tafiri , a Pan-African luxury fashion house founded in Lagos in 2010, has unveiled REVERIE, its Spring/Summer 2027 (SS27) collection, at an exclusive private showcase in Lagos on Sunday, October 25, 2026, held alongside Lagos Fashion Week. The showcase brought together distinguished guests, fashion industry leaders, patrons and representatives of the British Council Nigeria, including chef and media personality Hilda Baci, for a presentation of the house’s latest collection. REVERIE explores renewal and reinvention through contemporary African luxury. Bringing together expressive silhouettes, intricate craftsmanship and a refined colour palette, the collection presents a visual statement that celebrates the evolving language of African fashion. Through considered design and craftsmanship, REVERIE reflects the house’s continued exploration of contemporary African aesthetics, presenting pieces that balance creative expression with the distinctive design sensibility for which Ejiro Amos Tafiri is known. Founded by designer Ejiro Amos Tafiri, popularly known as Nigeria’s Drape Queen, the fashion house has spent 16 years developing a distinctive identity within the luxury fashion landscape. Its design language is characterised by expressive drapery, fluid tailoring and the thoughtful use of indigenous textiles, bringing African craftsmanship into contemporary fashion. The Lagos unveiling followed the third edition of Fashioning a Legacy: Leaving a Mark in Time, held on Saturday, October 24, 2026, at the British Council in Ikoyi, Lagos. The conference brought together designers, stylists, retail professionals and emerging creatives to discuss building sustainable careers and creating lasting impact within the fashion industry. Together, the events reflect Ejiro Amos Tafiri’s continued engagement with the broader creative ecosystem, connecting fashion, education, craftsmanship and the development of emerging talent. The REVERIE presentation forms part of the house’s 16-year milestone and will be followed by an exclusive showcase in Abuja on November 21, 2026. The forthcoming event will bring together members of the diplomatic community, government officials, fashion patrons and invited guests for a further presentation of the house’s work. As Ejiro Amos Tafiri looks towards its next chapter, REVERIE embodies an ongoing exploration of renewal and reinvention, reinforcing the house’s commitment to advancing contemporary African luxury through expressive design and intricate craftsmanship.
